label: Development stand-in, not a candidate. Proves the kit end to end; never evaluated and never counted toward a gate in docs/plan.md.

cold.load_includes: the worker's sha256 check of every pinned file, then the model load
cold.tor_bootstrap_includes: tor's start, with the state it saved in its lasting folder on earlier starts (none on its first), to its 'Bootstrapped 100% (done)' line; the host starts tor once the worker is ready and the guest once tor has bootstrapped. None: tor never bootstrapped, and the host stopped it at its 90 s limit or it exited
cold.first_result_includes: the cold load, tor's bootstrap, the guest's boot and the first call

manual_steps.how: Start `feasibility`, close the lid (or choose Sleep) during an EVAL06 call, wake after 60 s; note whether the call and the next ones finish, and attach the record of that run.
Run `feasibility` on battery with no other heavy apps, noting the battery percentage before and after and Activity Monitor's Energy column for cloak-rewriter.
State the ordinary Mac load the run had (apps open, other work running); the record holds only load average, memory and swap.
Rerun with memory pressure raised to warning by other apps (Activity Monitor's Memory Pressure graph turns yellow); note swap and any stopped calls.
Run `feasibility` first thing after restarting the Mac, so the model is read from disk rather than the file cache; compare the cold load.

not_measured: The full stack: the guest runs the daemon's local API and has Pi in the reference wrapper, and the host runs tor for it on the public Tor network, but there is no cover traffic or payment vault yet, and this kit's calls come from the daemon's rewrite code, not from Pi; so 'with the full stack loaded' (stage 3's exit condition) is not met by any record from this kit.
The daemon's full serve path: its payment vault is not deployed at the pinned commit; the kit drives the daemon's rewrite code as its client does before target inference (A11 stays open).
Per-process GPU use: macOS gives it only to root; the record has the system-wide GPU utilisation.

messages.content:
Review the following paragraph for clarity and suggest a shorter version that keeps every fact and number:

The quarterly survey, which was sent to all 412 registered volunteers in the second week of September and which closed on the last day of that month, received 187 complete responses, which is a response rate of about 45 percent, slightly higher than the 41 percent we saw in the spring survey, although the spring survey was only open for ten days rather than three weeks, so the two figures are not directly comparable. Most respondents, 132 of the 187, said they wanted more weekend shifts, and a smaller but notable group, around a fifth, said the online sign-up page was confusing, particularly on phones, where the calendar does not fit on the screen. Several people also mentioned that reminders arrived too late to be useful, often on the morning of the shift itself, and three suggested a text message the day before instead of an email. A handful of volunteers who had left during the year answered too, because the list had not been updated, and their answers were kept in the totals. Finally, the free-text answers were read by two people separately, and they agreed on the main themes.

messages.content: I'm going back and forth on whether to buy a used car or keep taking the bus and renting when I need one, and honestly I'd love an outside view because my friends all have strong opinions and none of them agree. Right now I spend about 95 euros a month on a bus pass and maybe rent a car four or five times a year, which costs around 70 euros a day, usually for two days at a time. The car I've been looking at is eight years old, has about 110,000 km on it, costs 6,500 euros, and the insurance quote was 540 euros a year. Parking near my flat is another 40 euros a month, and the yearly road tax would be about 180 euros. I'd probably drive it at weekends and for the odd trip to see family, about two hours away each way, maybe once a month. If I had the car I'd still keep the bus pass for getting to work, because parking at the office is a nightmare. I know there's fuel and repairs on top, and I have no idea how much to set aside for those on a car that age. I'd pay for it from savings, not a loan. Can you help me compare the yearly costs of both options in a simple table, say how much the car might be worth after three years, and tell me what assumptions you had to make? I don't want a lecture about the environment, just the numbers.

texts: Compare the yearly costs of a used car versus a bus pass and rental car, presenting the results in a simple table. Calculate the estimated value of the car after three years based on depreciation assumptions. State the assumptions used for the cost projections and the value estimation.

messages.content: Hi, I'm cooking for a family get-together on Sunday, twelve people in total, and it's turning into a bit of a puzzle, so any help would be amazing. My sister is coeliac so anything with gluten is out for her, and she's careful about cross-contamination too, so I can't just pick croutons off a salad. My brother-in-law doesn't eat pork, and my aunt is trying to avoid dairy at the moment, although a little butter in something cooked is fine for her. Two of the kids are very picky and basically only eat pasta, chicken and cucumber, and one of them refuses anything green that isn't cucumber. I was thinking of a big main that everyone can share plus a couple of sides, and something simple for dessert that doesn't need an oven, because the oven will be busy with the main. I'd like to prepare as much as possible on Saturday, since on Sunday morning I'll have to tidy up and pick my parents up from the station around eleven. Lunch should be on the table by one. I have one large oven, four rings on the hob and a slow cooker. Could you suggest a menu that works for all of them, say which dishes the picky kids can eat, and give me a rough timeline for Saturday and Sunday? Nothing fancy, I'm a decent cook but not a chef.

Schedule preparation for Saturday, with cleanup and parent pickup on Sunday morning. Ensure lunch is served by one PM. Utilize one large oven, four hob rings, and a slow cooker. messages.content: I'm planning a small vegetable garden, about 3 by 4 metres, in a spot that gets sun only in the morning. What could grow well there?
Leafy greens such as lettuce, spinach and chard, plus peas, radishes and herbs like parsley and mint, cope well with morning sun and afternoon shade.
ok nice. how far apart should I plant the lettuce and the peas? I don't want them crowding each other
Lettuce about 25 cm apart in rows 30 cm apart; peas about 5 cm apart along a support, with 60 cm between rows.
The soil is heavy clay. Should I dig in compost first, or build raised beds instead? Budget is around 150 euros.
Either works. Compost improves clay over a season or two; raised beds give good soil at once. Two simple 1.2 by 2.4 metre beds fit that budget if you build them yourself.
Let's go with raised beds. Give me a shopping list with rough prices, and say how much soil I need to fill them 30 cm deep.

texts: Generate a shopping list for raised beds with estimated rough prices per item, and calculate the required soil volume in cubic meters to fill the beds to a depth of 30 centimeters.
